ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is a point on the straight line $AB$, $\angle DOB=90^\circ$, $\angle EOC=90^\circ$. If $\angle DOE=50^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle BOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the given conditions, we have \\
$\because \angle BOC + \angle COD = 90^\circ$, \\
$\angle COD + \angle DOE = 90^\circ$, \\
$\therefore \angle BOC = \angle DOE = \boxed{50^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, AB is a horizontal straight line, point O is on AB, ray OB points to the right, and ray OA points to the left; from O upward there is ray OD, to the upper right there is ray OC, and to the upper left there is ray OE. Observing the order of the rays in the upper half-plane, from right to left they are successively OB, OC, OD, OE. The figure also marks the right-angle relationship with O as the vertex, corresponding to the given condition ∠DOB=90°, and combined with the given conditions ∠EOC=90° and ∠DOE=50°. Reasoning: Let x=∠COD. Because OC is located inside ∠DOB, and ∠DOB=90°, ∠BOC+x=90°. Also because OD is located inside ∠EOC, and ∠EOC=90°, and ∠DOE=50°, x+∠DOE=90°, that is, x+50°=90°, obtaining x=40°. Therefore ∠BOC=90°-40°=50°.
